⚡️ US lacks moral or legal standing to demand reopening of Strait of Hormuz: Iran

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei says Iran’s move to close the shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was in response to the continued US aggressive actions against the country, arguing that Washington has no moral or legal standing to demand the reopening of the strategic waterway.

Baqaei made the remarks during his weekly press briefing on Monday, in response to a question about the New York Times’ claims based on a list of Iran’s demands and their impact on the strait's reopening, as well as issues such as compensation, lifting of the Yemen blockade, withdrawal of American forces, and updating the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.
​
He said the American media construct was more aimed at whitewashing the key issue, that is, the reason behind the current situation of the Strait of Hormuz, which was open from the time of the creation of Adam until the illegal and unprovoked US–Israeli aggression in March.
​
Despite the decades of cruel and unfair Western sanctions on Iran, he continued, the Islamic Republic, being the guardian of the Strait of Hormuz, never obstructed the vessels carrying a significant part of the world's energy through this waterway.
​
Let us not forget that the problems that arose for Hormuz were the result of the US–Israeli military aggression, Baqaei reiterated, adding that if the Americans were concerned about the current situation, they should refer to their own government that proudly announced besieging Iranian ports and attacking Iranian ships.
​
In these circumstances, the spokesperson said, the US had no moral or legal standing to complain about the closure of the strait, since it is a US-created problem, and as long as the American violations continue, there will be no change in the status quo.
​
Baqaei also rejected any differences in opinions in the country’s executive and legislative branches on the negotiations between Iran and Oman on the Strait of Hormuz, saying that the governing institutions, including the Foreign Ministry and the Supreme National Security Council, are fully coordinated with the Parliament.
​
He said the parliament’s draft bill on managing the Strait of Hormuz is currently being reviewed, in the presence of the diplomatic apparatus, stressing that close communication and consultation would certainly help advance national interests.
​
Baqaei added that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had a very useful and valuable meeting with members of the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission of the Parliament on the day to discuss and review a wide range of issues.
​
The Foreign Ministry spokesperson also referred to documents on the US crimes, including the use of banned weapons in the bombing of Lamerd, saying the file has been delivered to international relevant authorities.
​
He said the legal pursuit of the crimes committed by the US and the Israeli regime against Iran in the past year is also on the agenda of a joint team from the Foreign Ministry and Judiciary, but the actions first require domestic trials before raising the issue in international courts and authorities.
​
Baqaei also pointed to the process of documentation by the Ministry of Health regarding the inhumane crime and the use of prohibited weapons by the United States, saying Iran has already reflected this to human rights authorities and relevant international institutions and will follow up seriously.
​
In response to a question about talks with the United States, Baqaei said he himself and even Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi have clarified numerously that there were no negotiations with Washington.

Crypto Idea

Long-Term investing strategy

When the crypto market is falling, buying feels scary. When it's going up, it feels like you've already missed your chance.

As a result, most people either buy based on emotion or keep waiting for the perfect entry point — and end up doing nothing at all.

But there's a simple way to avoid this problem: invest a fixed amount of money at regular intervals.

This strategy is called DCA (Dollar-Cost Averaging).

You simply choose the asset, the amount you want to invest, and how often you want to buy.

For example:
$50 worth of Bitcoin every week.

When Bitcoin is cheaper, your $50 buys more. When it's more expensive, it buys less. Over time, your average purchase price naturally evens out, and over the course of a few years, it often ends up being better than the average market participant's.

Bybit even has a built-in Auto-Invest bot designed specifically for this strategy. You set it up once — choose your currency, the coin, the investment amount, and the schedule.

After that, your purchases happen automatically, whether it's every day or once a month. The key is to choose a coin you genuinely believe in for the long term.

📌 RPC Nodes: Why Wallets Don’t Talk to Blockchains Directly

Main Points
⏺ Wallets usually connect through RPC nodes instead of reading the chain themselves
⏺ Node quality affects speed, reliability, and data accuracy
⏺ This post explains why “the network is lagging” can actually mean infrastructure trouble

1️⃣ What It Is — an RPC node handles wallet/app requests: balances, history, and transaction submission.
2️⃣ Why It Exists — most users don’t run full nodes, so interfaces rely on external infrastructure.
3️⃣ Risk Surface — nodes can lag, fail, filter data, or return incomplete results.
4️⃣ Privacy Angle — node providers may see which addresses and IPs are making requests.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — use reliable providers, switch endpoints during issues, and verify important data in explorers.

Final Thoughts

An RPC node is the bridge between your wallet and the chain. If that bridge is weak, the blockchain may be fine while your experience breaks.

📌 Tether Q2 profit hits $1.5B as USDT supply grows 

⚠️ Tether generated approximately $1.5 billion in net operating profit during the second quarter of 2026 as returns from US Treasury holdings and repo operations supported its earnings. The figures appeared in Tether’s latest reserve attestation, prepared by accounting firm BDO and released Friday. US government-backed securities continued to account for the largest portion of the company’s reserve portfolio. 

🌐 Interest earned from that portfolio, along with returns from repo operations, provided the main source of Tether’s second-quarter profit. The company’s exposure to short-term US debt has made its earnings sensitive to Federal Reserve policy and changes in Treasury yields. Tether also reported that the circulating supply of USDT reached approximately $184.6 billion by the end of June. Based on the company’s figures, the token controlled more than 60% of the global stablecoin market.

🔗 Tether adjusted the composition of its reserves during the quarter by reducing secured lending and increasing its holdings of physical gold. Outstanding secured loans fell by about $2.4 billion. Tether did not provide a full breakdown of the borrowers or collateral involved in the lending reduction in the information accompanying the results.

"Introduction to Machine Learning" is another free textbook on machine learning, approximately 600 pages long, which emphasizes a deep mathematical understanding of the subject. 📚🧮

The book begins with the mathematical foundations necessary for further study: linear algebra, mathematical analysis, probability theory, matrix analysis, and optimization methods. It then covers the main supervised learning algorithms: linear and logistic regression, the k-nearest neighbors method, decision trees, random forests, boosting, and neural networks. 🤖📈

A significant portion of the book is dedicated to probabilistic and generative models. It discusses Monte Carlo methods, graphical models, Bayesian networks, variational methods, normalizing flows, variational autoencoders (VAEs), and generative adversarial networks (GANs). 🎲🧠

The final chapters discuss clustering, principal component analysis (PCA), learning on manifolds, and theoretical estimates of a model's ability to generalize. 🔍📊

In my opinion, this is an excellent resource for those who want to gain a broad understanding of machine learning and understand the mathematics underlying the key methods, rather than treating them as "black boxes." 💡✨

A woman has defended journalist Larry Madowo amid criticism over his attendance at the wedding of President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene.

In a video circulating online, she argued that Larry’s decision to attend the wedding should not automatically undermine his work as a journalist or his criticism of the government.

The debate intensified after some netizens questioned how Larry could attend an event involving the President while also being vocal about political and governance issues.

Several people in the comments, however, defended his position, arguing that journalists can interact with political leaders and attend public or private events without abandoning their professional responsibilities or personal principles. #larrymadowo 🎥waakili
